intro: Covers the US session of Friday 16 October (Europe's close was not separately sourced). Gold's daily change could not be resolved between sources and is shown as not available.
footnotes: Index closes are for Friday 16 October; Nasdaq and Dow % changes are calculated from the point changes.
The 10-year yield is 5.09% (AP, Trading Economics; one source shows a +0.01 change, AP and others show -1 bp from 5.10%).
Gold: Trading Economics shows US$4,166.39 and FNArena US$4,173.22; sources conflict on the sign of the daily move (spot slightly lower vs futures up about 0.5%), so the change is not available.
AUD/USD and iron ore are CFD-based reference prices from a single source (Trading Economics).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are around 8,826, down about 0.1% (TradingView -0.12%; a New Zealand market wrap also points to a 0.1% lower open). That implies an ASX 200 open near 8,796, about 11 points or 0.12% lower. Investing.com showed the December contract down 0.23%, a slightly larger fall but the same direction. The ASX 200 closed Friday at 8,806.70, up 86.98 points (+1.00%), a near five-week high, and finished the week about 1% higher.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data release identified for today.
RBA Deputy Governor Hauser speaks Wednesday 21 October.
China's September activity data and Q3 GDP are due this week (exact date not confirmed).
what_moved: A broad AI and chip sell-off dominated Friday, with semiconductors falling for an eighth straight session and the Nasdaq posting its worst week since June (-4.5%). Rising oil added to the unease as Brent gained for a seventh session on Middle East supply risk. Energy (+2.52%), utilities (+1.34%) and consumer staples (+1.08%) led the S&P 500; technology (-3.03%) and communication services (-1.89%) lagged. The VIX jumped to 19.99.

news.headline: Chip rout caps worst week since June
news.summary: The Nasdaq fell 4.5% and the S&P 500 about 2% on the week, while the Dow gained 0.7%; AMD, Intel and Micron each lost roughly 6%.

news.headline: Oil extends its run above US$100
news.summary: Brent gained about 3.7% to roughly US$109.9/bbl and WTI about US$101.7, with Iranian tanker attacks and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries sustaining a supply premium.

news.headline: Fed Chair Warsh gives no rate signal
news.summary: Markets price about a 17% chance of a hike at the late-October meeting and about 89% for December, with the question pushed out to December.

news.headline: Hot inflation prints keep yields high
news.summary: Hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI data sent the 10-year yield to 5.33% on Wednesday before it eased to 5.09% on Friday.

news.headline: Soft Australian jobs data trims RBA hike bets
news.summary: September employment fell 39,000 and unemployment rose to 4.7%; the next RBA meeting is 3 November and Q3 CPI is due 28 October.

news.headline: ASX 200 rallies 1% on Friday
news.summary: Banks and a BHP-Escondida wage deal that averted a strike lifted the index; gains were capped ahead of China data.

news.headline: AI capex worries build
news.summary: Microsoft reportedly exited a UK data-centre deal with Nscale and CoreWeave fell about 12% on debt concerns, ahead of Meta, Tesla and other earnings.

news.headline: Weak week for Asian tech-heavy markets
news.summary: Japan's Nikkei fell 5.4% over the week while the FTSE 100 gained 3.1% to 10,881.90.

coming_up: Wednesday 21 October: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser speaks, and UK CPI is due. Big-tech earnings (including Meta and Tesla) land later this week and next; Australian Q3 CPI follows on 28 October, ahead of the Fed's late-October meeting and the RBA on 3 November.
